summary: Pass (third and final critique pass; bounce cap spent). All three faults from pass 2 are confirmed fixed by measurement in a real browser, not by re-reading the spec: card surfaces sampled from the render give INK rgb(23,18,15) < Windows rgb(29,25,21) < macOS rgb(36,30,27), so the hierarchy inversion is provably gone; the metadata renders the literal unresolved placeholder 'macOS ⟨MIN VERSION — TBC⟩' rather than an invented number; and the new in-context render shows the light→dark Pricing seam landing cleanly and the Download orb reading as a quiet setup for the Closing CTA's brighter bloom. Accessibility tree confirms the Windows card contains zero focusable nodes (the strongest decision in the section), metadata contrast measures 5.94:1 against the brightened macOS surface, the download button is 51px tall with a correct accessible name, and both cards' action and metadata rows are baseline-locked at 1440px and 390px. Two minor, non-blocking faults remain and are documented with one-line fixes rather than bounced: the Windows action row inherits the macOS button's 24px horizontal padding and so sits 24px off the card's left rail (three left edges in one card, most visible at 390px), and that card's centered metadata line has no full-width element above it justifying the centering. escalate is set to true so the orchestrator surfaces to Jacey the items this pipeline deliberately did not close: two blocking /build placeholders (hosted .dmg URL, real minimum macOS version), the doubled-dark-run judgment call (280px of uninterrupted dark between Download and Closing CTA vs. ~180px at the page's existing dark seam, with an asymmetric-bottom-padding fix offered), and the design's deliberate override of intake's stroke-icon desirable in favour of filled brand glyphs.
